q: sky blue during day red at sunset
why is the sky blue during the day but red at sunset
why sky is blue and red at sunset
sky blue daytime red sunset explanation
why is the sky blue and sunset red
why sky appears blue at day and red at sunset
a: The sky appears blue during the day and red at sunset due to a phenomenon called Rayleigh scattering. Sunlight is composed of all colors of visible light, each with a different wavelength. Blue light has a shorter wavelength and is scattered more strongly by the molecules in Earth's atmosphere (mainly nitrogen and oxygen). When the sun is high in the sky, the sunlight travels a relatively short path through the atmosphere. The shorter blue wavelengths are scattered in all directions by air molecules, making the entire sky appear blue from our perspective. At sunrise and sunset, the sun is near the horizon, and sunlight must travel through a much thicker layer of atmosphere. The increased path length causes even more scattering, but the blue light is scattered so much that it is largely removed from the direct sunlight. The longer wavelengths (red, orange, yellow) are scattered less and pass through the atmosphere more directly, reaching our eyes as the dominant colors. This is why sunsets and sunrises appear red, orange, and pink. The same principle also explains why the sky appears pale blue or white near the horizon during the day, and why clouds (which contain larger water droplets that scatter all wavelengths equally) appear white.
